doc.title: Kenny Burrell — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Coltrane, Jimmy Smith and musical values
title: Personnel and tune on the Burrell-Coltrane Prestige album
summary: Brown and Burrell sort out personnel and the origin of the title Lyresto.

story.theme_name: Playing with Coltrane and the avant-garde

blocks.x: Yeah, you had two different, no, you had two different sessions. One with you, Trane, Tommy Flanagan, Paul Chambers, Jimmy Cobb.
And there was the other one that was originally released as two trumpet and two tenors, Interplay for, and that was Idrees Sulieman, and…
So that was an earlier session.
Well, this one was with Jimmy Cobb.
Yeah, yeah. Kimery: Lets just pause for one second.
And we’re back to the Kenny Burrell, John Coltrane Prestige recording, and on here there is only one original by you. “Lyresto”, is that the correct pronunciation?
So what was the inspiration for that and the title, it’s a very, I thought it was “Liar-esto”, but I wanted to get that clarification from you.
I think I was thinking about it being lyrical, and I think I probably didn’t spell it right.
Well, at least you get the royalties for it, it’s your tune. [laughs]
